why.historical_trend: Kayak’s median Atlanta–Mumbai round trip is $1,363 in December versus $707 in April (Kayak route data, read 17 Nov 2026). Google Flights calendar estimates from the same day show the same seasonal drop: one-way ATL–BOM around $1,460–$2,040 in mid-December, then a sharp decline after Christmas, with most mid-January to mid-February dates about $450–$540 (the low is $450 on 1 Feb). Kayak also puts the current average one-way ATL–BOM at about $487, 11% below its typical $412–$667 range. Kayak’s 1 Apr 2026 booking study finds international fares cheapest on average 7–14 days before departure (domestic 21–30 days). That average window is tight for a long-haul holiday-season trip; Kayak also says to book early for Christmas through New Year’s and to book when a fare meets your budget rather than waiting for a lower one that may not come.
why.fuel_outlook: Jet fuel and crude have been falling, not rising, over the past three to six weeks. IATA’s Jet Fuel Price Monitor (checked 17 Nov 2026) puts the global average at $169.82 a barrel last week, down 5.1% from the week before — the third straight weekly decline from about $196.70 in late October. That is still far above pre-conflict levels (IATA $94.97/bbl for the week ending 30 Jan 2026). The EIA U.S. Gulf Coast jet-fuel spot was $4.035/gal on 11 Nov 2026, down from a recent high of $4.686/gal on 23 Oct (EIA via FRED, retrieved 17 Nov 2026). Brent was about $92/bbl early on 17 Nov 2026 (CNBC, 17 Nov 2026, 0102 GMT), down from $103.60 on 3 Nov and from a North Sea Dated high of $136 on 8 Oct (IEA Oil Market Report, 13 Nov 2026). The EIA Short-Term Energy Outlook (released 10 Nov 2026; inputs frozen 5 Nov, so it misses the mid-November drop) forecasts Brent near $100/bbl for the rest of 2026, then $94.90 in Q1 2027 and $85.78 as the 2027 average, with U.S. wholesale jet fuel easing from $4.09/gal in Q4 2026 to $3.71 in Q1 2027. Goldman Sachs (note cited by CNBC, 16 Nov 2026) expects Brent to average $88 in 2027 and $78 by year-end. Airline surcharges are still elevated: Air India $215 one-way on North America sectors (revised 9 Oct 2026) and Emirates $322 economy one-way to the Americas (effective 1 Nov 2026). Gulf shipping attacks continue, and EASA extended Middle East airspace warnings on 16 Nov 2026 through 31 Jan 2027. Implication: falling fuel gives some room to wait for a sale; still-high fuel, surcharges, and geopolitical volatility are not a reason to wait past mid-December.
why.verdict: Round trip: this is a book-now signal. Skyscanner on 17 Nov 2026 showed Turkish Airlines at $849 (27 Jan–27 Apr 2027, one stop in Istanbul each way), bookable direct with Turkish and at the ≤ $850 line. Confirm 2×23 kg checked bags before paying. Qatar + IndiGo at $846 on the same dates is equivalent in price but was listed via third-party sites — prefer qatarairways.com if the fare matches. One-way: the call is unchanged. The best reliable single-ticket fares now are $499–$516, around or just above the $500 line, so wait through Black Friday / Cyber Monday (27–30 Nov 2026) unless you want to take the $499 two-stop now, and plan to book by about 10 Dec for January travel. Ignore Skyscanner one-way calendar lows in the $368–$419 range when they are long self-transfers or Ethiopian. Avoid departing before about 26 Dec unless the dates are fixed: that is peak pricing. Fuel is still easing, which is why one-way can wait for the sale window; the round-trip threshold has already been met.

notes: Hyderabad dropped: Mumbai was cheaper on every date checked (17 Nov 2026).

Skyscanner (read 17 Nov 2026, about 9:49 AM IST, USD, 1 adult economy) produced a book-now round trip: Turkish $849, 27 Jan–27 Apr 2027, one stop in Istanbul, bookable direct with Turkish. Qatar + IndiGo was $846 on the same dates via third-party sites; prefer qatarairways.com if the price matches. Skyscanner’s cheapest one-way calendar prices ($368–$419) are mostly self-transfer itineraries (Frontier + Etihad/Royal Jordanian via IAD, 40–50 hours) or Ethiopian ($419) and are not recommended. The best reliable single-ticket one-ways on that scan were United + SWISS $499 (20 Jan, 2 stops) and Lufthansa $516 (13 Feb, 1 stop FRA).

December is the peak. Kayak’s median Atlanta–Mumbai round trip is $1,363 in December versus $707 in April (Kayak, read 17 Nov 2026). On the Google calendar, mid-December one-ways are roughly three to four times the mid-January prints. Avoid departing before about 26 Dec unless the dates are fixed.

Airline reliability (OAG on-time performance, October 2026): SAS 86.4%, Air India 80.5%, Lufthansa 78.5%, Gulf Air 77.3% (but 5.7% cancellations), Emirates 74.4%, Qatar 73.4%, Etihad 72.3%, British Airways 71.6%, KLM 71.2% (3.8% cancellations), Ethiopian 59.8% — a clear caution on the cheap Ethiopian round trip.

Checked bags vary by fare brand, which is why a headline price can disappoint. Qatar Classic+ 2×23 kg (Lite 1×23); Etihad Value+ 2×23 kg (Basic none); Air India Classic/Flex 2×23 kg (Value 1×23); Emirates Saver+ 2×23 kg (Special 1×23); Lufthansa economy typically 1×23 kg; Air France economy often 0–1×23 kg. Confirm bags before buying a ‘basic’ or ‘lite’ fare, especially for a move.

Transit visas for an Indian passport: a UK airside transit visa is needed unless an exemption applies (for example a valid US visa). Germany has not required an airport transit visa since 3 Jun 2026. France is not on the ATV list. Amsterdam and Copenhagen transit rules were not verified in this scan — check before buying a SAS or KLM itinerary.

Jet fuel has fallen for three straight weeks (IATA global average $169.82/bbl last week, down 5.1%; EIA US Gulf Coast jet $4.035/gal on 11 Nov, down from $4.686 on 23 Oct) and official outlooks point lower into 2027, but prices remain well above pre-conflict levels and Gulf airspace/shipping risk is still active (EASA warnings extended 16 Nov 2026 through 31 Jan 2027). Air India still levies a $215 North America fuel surcharge (from 9 Oct 2026); Emirates $322 economy to the Americas (from 1 Nov 2026).
No US–India Black Friday / Cyber Monday sale had been announced as of 17 Nov 2026 (Lufthansa had only published a teaser). The 27–30 Nov window is still worth watching.
Prices on this page are research snapshots, not a booking confirmation. Google calendar figures are estimates. Always re-check the live fare, bags, layover type, and visa rules before paying.
